items.followUp: Write two characteristics of kingdom Plantae.

rubric.why: A correct property of fungi is identified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fungi are eukaryotic or have a true nucleus.

rubric.why: A second correct property of fungi is identified.
rubric.description: Fungi are heterotrophic, lack chlorophyll, or have cell walls made of chitin.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these properties, distinct from the first.

modelAnswer: They are heterotrophic and their cell walls contain chitin.

items.followUp: Name two endangered animal species found in Pakistan.

rubric.why: One endangered species in Pakistan is named.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the Indus dolphin.

rubric.why: A second endangered species in Pakistan is named.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the snow leopard.

modelAnswer: The Indus river dolphin is an endangered species in Pakistan.
The snow leopard is another endangered species in Pakistan.

items.followUp: State two functions of the cell wall.

rubric.why: The membrane's role in controlling exchange is stated.
rubric.description: The cell membrane regulates the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it controls or regulates substances entering or leaving the cell.

rubric.why: A second function of the membrane is stated.
rubric.description: The cell membrane forms the boundary of the cell and separates its contents from the surroundings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its boundary or protective role.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane regulates the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
It forms the cell’s boundary and separates the cell contents from the surroundings.

items.followUp: State two functions of the nucleus.

rubric.why: A digestive role of lysosomes is identified.
rubric.description: Lysosomes digest waste materials and foreign particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that lysosomes digest waste or foreign material.

rubric.why: A second function of lysosomes is identified.
rubric.description: Lysosomes break down worn-out cell parts and may bring about autolysis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing breakdown of worn-out organelles or autolysis.

modelAnswer: Lysosomes digest waste materials and foreign particles in the cell.
They break down worn-out organelles and can cause autolysis.

items.followUp: Define mitosis and describe what happens to the cytoplasm during cell division.

rubric.why: Karyokinesis is defined as division of the nucleus.
rubric.description: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the nucleus divides.

rubric.why: Cytokinesis is defined as division of the cytoplasm.
rubric.description: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cytoplasm divides.

modelAnswer: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.

rubric.description: Apoptosis is programmed, controlled cell death.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying apoptosis as programmed or controlled cell death.

rubric.description: Necrosis is uncontrolled cell death caused by injury or damage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying necrosis as uncontrolled or damage-related cell death.

modelAnswer: Apoptosis is programmed and controlled cell death.
Necrosis is uncontrolled cell death that occurs due to injury or damage.

items.followUp: What are the gametophyte and sporophyte generations?

rubric.why: The life cycle is described as alternating between two generations.
rubric.description: The life cycle alternates between gametophyte and sporophyte generations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the regular alternation of the two generations.

rubric.why: The ploidy of the generations is correctly stated.
rubric.description: The gametophyte is haploid and the sporophyte is diploid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the haploid and diploid generations.

modelAnswer: Alternation of generations is the regular alternation of gametophyte and sporophyte generations in an organism’s life cycle.
The gametophyte is haploid, while the sporophyte is diploid.

items.followUp: What is a substrate, and how does it interact with an enzyme?

rubric.why: The active site is identified as a particular region of the enzyme.
rubric.description: The active site is a specific region or part of an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a specific region of the enzyme.

rubric.why: The role of the active site is explained.
rubric.description: The substrate binds to the active site, where the reaction takes place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the substrate binds there or that the reaction occurs there.

modelAnswer: The active site is a specific region of an enzyme.
The substrate binds to this site, where the enzyme-catalysed reaction takes place.
